name: Baniva de Maroa
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2001. Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional: Comparação e Descrição. Manaus: Editora da Universidade do Amazonas (EDUA).
catalog_locator: Ch.7 'Divisão Alto Orinoco', §7.2 'Fonologia' (Baniva de Maroa), pp.504-505
catalog_quote: O acento é contrastivo em Baniva de Maroa, várias sílabas da mesma palavra podendo ter um tom alto. Exemplos de oposição: éma anta / emá grita; náwa minha perna / nawá toma banho; pínaṣi remédio / pináṣi povoado; wápiṣi lábio / wapíṣi nossa cauda. González Ñáñez apresenta um sistema acentual muito complexo, com acento agudo (´), acento grave (`), acento circunflexo (^) e acento inflexo (ˇ), com 3 níveis de altura tonal! Não concordamos com esta análise, o sistema podendo simplesmente ser descrito com uma oposição entre um tom alto marcado e um tom baixo não marcado. Por exemplo: GRAFIA DE G.N. / MINHA GRAFIA: âatapi / áatapi árvore; úulu / úulú aranha; wíminali / wímínálí estrela; wabùupi / wabúpi igarapé; nuwèjá / nuwejá quero.

Exemplos de oposição: éma anta / emá grita; náwa minha perna / nawá toma banho; pínaṣi remédio / pináṣi povoado; wápiṣi lábio / wapíṣi nossa cauda. González Ñáñez apresenta um sistema acentual muito complexo, com acento agudo ( ´ ), acento grave ( ` ), acento circunflexo ( ^ ) e acento inflexo ( ˇ ), com 3 níveis de altura tonal! Não concordamos com esta análise, o sistema podendo simplesmente ser descrito com uma oposição entre um tom alto marcado e um tom baixo não marcado.
new_statements.translation: Accent is contrastive in Baniva de Maroa; several syllables of the same word may bear a high tone. Examples of opposition: éma 'tapir' / emá 'shouts'; náwa 'my leg' / nawá 'bathes'; pínaṣi 'medicine' / pináṣi 'village'; wápiṣi 'lip' / wapíṣi 'our tail'. González Ñáñez presents a very complex accentual system, with acute, grave, circumflex and 'inflex' accents and 3 levels of pitch height! We do not agree with this analysis; the system can simply be described as an opposition between a marked high tone and an unmarked low tone.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: Ramirez 2001 (author-shared open PDF, ->) ch.7 'A divisao Alto Orinoco', sec. 7.2 'Fonologia', printed p.504-505 (pdf 514-515). Verified in the text ( lines 21084-21107) and on the page renders /: 'O acento e contrastivo em Baniva de Maroa, varias silabas da mesma palavra podendo ter um tom alto. Exemplos de oposicao: ema anta / ema grita; nawa minha perna / nawa toma banho; pinasi remedio / pinasi povoado; wapisi labio / wapisi nossa cauda' [accents as quoted by the compiler: éma/emá, náwa/nawá, pínaṣi/pináṣi, wápiṣi/wapíṣi], then 'Gonzalez Nanez apresenta um sistema acentual muito complexo, com acento agudo, acento grave, acento circunflexo e acento inflexo, com 3 niveis de a…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No positional stress rule: the place of the accent (high pitch) is lexically contrastive (éma vs emá etc.), and more than one syllable of a word may carry the marked high tone; Ramirez analyses the prosody as a privative high (marked) vs low (unmarked) tone opposition rather than a fixed stress. Aikhenvald (2012:7 'A acentuação é contrastiva'; 1999:79 'Stress is contrastive . WX') describes the same facts as contrastive lexical stress, so a placement-only coding would be lexical (unpredictable).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress; Ramirez's examples show several high-toned syllables in one word (wímínálí 'star', úulú 'spider') rather than a primary/secondary hierarchy.
new_statements.exceptions: None as exceptions; Ramirez notes vowel length is also contrastive (úpe vs úpee) and disputes González Ñáñez's (1996) four-accent, three-level notation. Venezuelan descriptions (Mosonyi & Camico 1996; Álvarez & Socorro 2002 'rico sistema de tonos', 'configuración tonal Medio-Alto-Bajo') treat the system as tonal.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level citation forms (isolated lexical items with Ramirez's own field transcription). Analyses conflict on category, not on facts: contrastive stress (Aikhenvald 1998/1999/2012) vs marked-H/unmarked-L tone (Ramirez 2001) vs multi-level tone/accent (González Ñáñez 1996; Mosonyi & Camico 1996/2000; SAPhon codes 'Tone').
new_statements.identity_note: Ramirez 2001 ch.7 describes Baniva de Maroa as spoken in and around Maroa, Venezuela (Glottolog dialect bani1260 'Baniva de Guainia'); Aikhenvald 1998/2012 describe Warekena of Xié, Brazil (ware1257), which both authors state is the same language with little dialectal difference (Xié communities founded by migrants from Maroa). Caution: the label 'Warekena/Guarequena' with the same ISO code gae is also used for OLD Warekena of Guzmán Blanco/San Miguel (González Ñáñez 1997, 2009 'Gramática warekena'; Ramirez 2001 §4.1; SAPhon 'Warekena' page, suprasegmental 'None'), a distinct North-Arawak language close to Mandawaka and not mutually intelligible with Baniva de Maroa (Aikhenvald 2012:3); statements from those works must not be attributed to guar1293's Baniva/Xié variety.

tone_statements.citation: Mosonyi, Esteban Emilio. 2002. La fonología suprasegmental y otras particularidades del baniva de Maroa, idioma tonal arawak del Río Negro, Venezuela. In Mily Crevels, Simon van de Kerke, Sérgio Meira & Hein van der Voort (eds.), Current Studies on South American Languages (Indigenous Languages of Latin America [ILLA], 3), 127-136. Leiden: Research School of Asian, African, and Amerindian Studies (CNWS), Universiteit Leiden.
tone_statements.quote: Existen tres acentos tonales fundamentales (conocemos por lo menos dos más, de poca ocurrencia), en cierta forma análogos a los que presentan el sueco y el noruego ... El agudo (´) indica que la sílaba acentuada se pronuncia en un nivel alto ... las inacentuadas que siguen, siempre débiles, mantienen exactamente el mismo nivel musical ... Con el acento grave (`) la sílaba acentuada se pronuncia fuerte y en un nivel bajo ... El tercer acento, llamado circunflejo (^), indica que la sílaba acentuada ... es alta y las inacentuadas, débiles, se desplazan al nivel medio o incluso bajo
tone_statements.translation: There are three fundamental tonal accents (we know of at least two more, of low occurrence), in a way analogous to those of Swedish and Norwegian ... The acute (´) indicates that the accented syllable is pronounced at a high level ... the unaccented ones that follow, always weak, keep exactly the same musical level ... With the grave accent (`) the accented syllable is pronounced strong and at a low level ... The third accent, called circumflex (^), indicates that the accented syllable ... is high and the unaccented ones, weak, move to the mid or even low level
tone_statements.locator: pp.130-131, body of the article (no section numbering)
tone_statements.summary: Three main 'tonal accents' (acute=high, grave=low, circumflex=high with post-tonic fall) plus 2+ rare ones; analysed as stress accents carrying pitch, cf. Swedish; 3sg.m marked by pitch alone.

sources.note: p.504-505: 'O acento é contrastivo em Baniva de Maroa, várias sílabas da mesma palavra podendo ter um tom alto' with minimal pairs (éma 'anta' vs emá 'grita', náwa vs nawá, pínaṣi vs pináṣi, wápiṣi vs wapíṣi); rejects González Ñáñez's 4-accent / 3-pitch-level system and re-describes it as marked high tone vs unmarked low tone (e.g. wímínálí 'estrela', áatapi 'árvore'). First-hand (Ramirez lists Baniva de Maroa among the languages he studied in the field).

sources.note: p.79 (family survey, second-hand): 'Stress is contrastive in some languages (Bau, Wa, Ya, Ba, WX, Acha), but not in others (Ca, Bhw). Nasalized or long vowels are often stressed.' WX = Warekena of Xié; WX is NOT listed among the pitch accent languages (Acha, Pia, Die, Ta).
